mcqs.q: Which strategies did most animal control officers agree were among the most effective for community engagement?
o: Relationship-building, providing assistance/information, and allowing time for compliance
Seizure of animals on first contact
mcqs.e: Officers identified relationship-building, assistance, and time for compliance as most effective.

mcqs.q: How consistent was the definition of community engagement across the officers studied?
mcqs.e: The phenomenology found definitions varied greatly across the sample.

mcqs.q: What did the authors recommend for future research and policymaking?
o: Establish a consistent definition that can then be optimized and evaluated
mcqs.e: They urged a consistent, evaluable definition of community engagement.

mcqs.q: According to the review, health benefits of companion animals are predicated mainly on what?
o: Human perceptions of the animal rather than its species
The purchase cost of the animal
mcqs.e: Benefits depended on human perceptions, not the species.

mcqs.q: What was a key gap the review identified?
o: Lack of rigorous research into non-conventional companion animals
mcqs.e: The literature lacked high-quality empirical research on these species.

mcqs.q: How might non-conventional companion animals benefit their guardians?
o: Providing social support and acting as attachment figures
mcqs.e: They may offer social support, routines, attachment, and restorative experiences.

mcqs.q: What did results suggest may reduce moral stress in charity veterinary hospitals?
mcqs.e: Facilitated ethical discussion groups appeared to reduce moral stress.

mcqs.q: Moral stress was attributed primarily to what?
o: Uncertainty about the ability to fulfill ethical obligations
mcqs.e: It stemmed from uncertainty about meeting ethical obligations.

mcqs.q: How did participants characterize moral stress?
mcqs.e: It was described as everyday and cumulative, interacting with other stress.

mcqs.q: A higher pre-treatment neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR > 5) was associated with what?
mcqs.e: NLR > 5 correlated with reduced survival after surgery.

mcqs.q: What was found about the albumin-to-globulin ratio (AGR) alone?
o: It was the strongest sole predictor
It showed no predictive value on malignancy by itself
mcqs.e: AGR alone did not predict tumor malignancy.

mcqs.q: What best predicted tumor grade and post-surgical survival?
o: Combining NLR, AGR, age, and tumor size in a principal component analysis
mcqs.e: A PCA combining NLR, AGR, age, and size predicted grade and survival.

mcqs.q: What was the overall health status of most shelter dogs in this study?
mcqs.e: Most dogs were apparently healthy despite some clinical changes.

mcqs.q: Which hematological alteration was most common?
mcqs.e: Thrombocytopenia (36.31%) was the most frequent finding.

mcqs.q: What was the vaccination and deworming coverage of the shelter population?
mcqs.e: All dogs were vaccinated and dewormed (100%).

mcqs.q: How do the AVMA 2020 Euthanasia Guidelines classify pentobarbital and its combination products?
o: Acceptable for all species when circumstances permit
mcqs.e: They are listed as acceptable for all species when circumstances permit.

mcqs.q: What risks arise from improper handling/disposal of pentobarbital-euthanized remains?
o: Relay toxicosis in wildlife and contamination of the food supply
mcqs.e: Improper disposal can cause relay toxicosis and food-supply contamination.

mcqs.q: What gap motivated this literature review?
o: No prior comprehensive review on pentobarbital euthanasia/disposal existed
mcqs.e: No comprehensive review on the topic had previously been published.

mcqs.q: How did microchipping rates compare between cats and dogs in Portugal?
o: Cats were microchipped more than dogs
Cats were far less microchipped (12%) than dogs (77%)
mcqs.e: Only 12% of cats vs 77% of dogs were microchipped.

mcqs.q: Animals acquired from municipal shelters or protection associations were more likely to be what?
mcqs.e: Shelter/association animals had higher odds of neutering and microchipping.

mcqs.q: Which finding about male neutering was reported?
o: Dogs neutered far more than cats
Male cats neutered more (74%) than male dogs (35%)
mcqs.e: Male cats (74%) were neutered more than male dogs (35%).

mcqs.q: Overall, how did dog foster volunteers feel about their organizations' support?
mcqs.e: Fosters were generally satisfied with the support provided.

mcqs.q: Which areas were fosters less positive about?
o: Communication, training beyond basics, and social support networks
mcqs.e: Gaps were in communication, advanced training, and social support networks.

mcqs.q: What was the survey sample size?
mcqs.e: The national survey had 611 respondents.

mcqs.q: What did the welfare education intervention significantly improve relative to controls?
mcqs.e: The intervention group improved significantly in emotion recognition.

mcqs.q: What happened to attitudes that cruelty is acceptable in the control group?
o: They improved in the control group
They worsened in the control group
They were unchanged in the control group
mcqs.e: Control-group attitudes toward cruelty worsened over time.

mcqs.q: What was the study's overall conclusion?
o: Age-appropriate welfare education can enhance emotion recognition and attitudes
mcqs.e: Age-appropriate humane education effectively improved recognition and attitudes.

mcqs.q: How did US and Japanese attitudes toward pet cats compare?
o: Japan was more positive than the US
US citizens were significantly more positive toward pet cats
mcqs.e: US attitudes toward pet cats were significantly more positive.

mcqs.q: What did the study find about owner attachment to cats?
o: Owners in both countries were highly attached
mcqs.e: Owners in both countries reported high attachment.

mcqs.q: How did cat proximity to people differ between countries?
o: Japanese cats spent more time near people
US pet and café cats spent a greater proportion of time near people
Cats avoided people in both countries
mcqs.e: US cats spent more time in proximity to people than Japanese cats.

mcqs.q: What main effect did the role-reversal speciesism intervention produce?
o: Increased intention to reduce harmful behavior toward animals
mcqs.e: The intervention strengthened intentions to reduce harmful behavior.

mcqs.q: What was the intervention's effect on speciesist attitudes and behavioral responses?
o: No effect on speciesist attitudes or behavioral responses
mcqs.e: There were no effects on attitudes or actual behavioral responses.

mcqs.q: What mediated the intervention's effect on intentions (Study 2)?
mcqs.e: Feelings of injustice mediated the effect on behavioral intentions.

mcqs.q: After accounting for life-course and lifestyle factors, how was dog ownership related to income, education, and occupation?
o: Not linked with income, education, or occupation
mcqs.e: Once life-course/lifestyle were controlled, family SEP showed no link.

mcqs.q: Which owners were more likely to have mixed-breed dogs?
o: Low-income owners with limited labor-market involvement
mcqs.e: Low-income, weakly labor-attached owners more often had mixed-breed dogs.

mcqs.q: Keeping a dog for social support was mainly observed among which group?
o: Lower-education owners who were often involuntarily alone
mcqs.e: Social-support motivation centered on lower-education, often-lonely owners.
